study_identification_part.si4_title: Unraveling the link between CNVs, cognition and individual neuroimaging deviation scores from a population-based reference cohort

study_characteristics_part.sc1_study_objective: To map individualized brain deviation scores in individuals with pathogenic copy number variations (CNVs) using normative modeling, and to examine the relationship between brain deviations and cognitive function at the individual level.

clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa7_association_analysis: Spearman rank correlation between total count of extreme deviation scores (|z| > 2) and general cognitive ability score (derived from first principal component of seven cognitive tests from UK Biobank); separate correlations for positive (z > 2) and negative (z < -2) deviations; correlation analysis with polygenic risk scores (PGS) for seven psychiatric disorders (ADHD, ASD, major depressive disorder, anxiety, schizophrenia, bipolar disorder, cannabis use disorder) using FDR correction (Benjamini-Hochberg method) for multiple comparisons; visual comparisons of deviation count distributions between CNV carriers and non-carriers using box plots and frequency distributions
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa8_key_findings_brief: Pathogenic CNV carriers showed high heterogeneity in brain deviation patterns at the individual level; negative deviations (z < -2) were significantly correlated with lower cognitive ability (r = -0.04, p = 0.04); 1q21.1 duplication carriers showed more negative deviations (volume contractions) while deletion carriers showed more positive deviations (volume expansions), consistent with known macrocephaly and microcephaly effects.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa9_key_findings_detailed: The study demonstrated substantial heterogeneity in brain deviation patterns among pathogenic CNV carriers at the individual level. Normative models for IDPs explained up to 50% of variance, while voxel-wise Jacobian models explained up to 52% of variance with acceptable model fit (|skew| < 1, kurtosis < 5). For 1q21.1 distal CNV carriers (n=5 deletion, n=5 duplication), deletion carriers showed more positive deviations (indicating smaller brain volumes relative to norms, consistent with microcephaly), while duplication carriers showed more negative deviations (indicating larger volumes, consistent with macrocephaly). Specific regions implicated included: for deletions, notable positive deviations in caudate and accumbens; for duplications, large negative deviations in cerebellum, brainstem, and pallidum. Aggregated analysis across 1q21.1dup carriers revealed substantial negative deviations in occipital cortex, while 1q21.1del carriers showed pronounced positive deviations in cerebellum and thalamus. Spearman correlation analysis revealed that higher counts of extreme negative deviations (z < -2) were significantly associated with lower general cognitive ability (r = -0.04, p = 0.04), while positive deviations showed no significant correlation (r = 0.03, p = 0.09). The findings were consistent with prior literature showing dose-response effects of 1q21.1 CNV on brain structure and cognition, while revealing substantial individual-level variability not captured in traditional case-control analyses.

clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa11_application_notes: Study emphasizes individual-level approach over traditional case-control framework; approach enables study of rare CNVs with small sample sizes (e.g., single carriers of 16p11.2 deletion/duplication); individual brain deviation maps presented alongside word clouds summarizing most implicated brain regions using Harvard cortical and subcortical atlas; aggregated deviation maps across carriers shown to compare with traditional case-control findings while demonstrating individual heterogeneity; deviation scores correlated with polygenic risk scores for multiple psychiatric disorders; models and code made publicly available via GitHub (PCNtoolkit and CNV_normative_modeling repositories)

general_note_part.gn1_general_notes: This study represents a novel application of normative modeling to understand individual-level effects of rare pathogenic CNVs. The paper notes that the publication year is 2024 (published online November 1, 2024) but the study ID uses author name 'Fraza' with year 2023 in some contexts. The study received ethical approval previously through contributing datasets, with UK Biobank data accessed under application 23668. The paper emphasizes moving from group-level to individual-level inferences in psychiatric genetics and proposes this as a starting point toward personalized psychiatry. Additional CNVs analyzed beyond 1q21.1 include 15q11.2, 16p11.2, and 16p13.11 deletions/duplications (presented in supplementary materials). The study is part of larger effort to understand Research Domain Criteria (RDoC) dimensional approaches to psychiatric disorders rather than categorical DSM-V classifications.
